prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias Juniper), 24/7 regional EMS dispatch: intake, triage, ambulance dispatch under clinical/jurisdictional protocols. Zones have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center. Center creates incident record, preserves caller report, escalates readiness gaps, produces Unit Staging Change Card, records authorization time, unit-selection reason, approved routes, maintains coverage picture; uses Battery Swap Voucher, North Approach Queue Snapshot, Caller Location Correction Slip; updates incident status on transfer confirmation. Mode: Surge operations, entered when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls or staffed unit availability cross policy thresholds; Center monitors continuously, declares surge level. Actors: Call Taker Mara (alias Larkspur): produces Caller Location Correction Slip; receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, verifies arrival time vs timeline. Triage Supervisor (alias Copperfield): assigns priority, validates surge declaration; sends Pediatric Acuity Note; pediatric ABC/mental-status concerns get prompt escalation. Regional Medical Director: clinical policy, surge clinical direction. Dispatcher: recommends units, checks coverage. Shift Commander (alias Sundial): approves exceptions; sends Mutual Aid Release Form; reviews access constraints; assigns surge roles; escalates unresolved destination/access issues; shall not override Medical Director or crew. Radio Coordinator (alias Mistral): transmits incident/destination info over Regional Radio Network; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Paramedic Crew: acknowledges, reports status, requests reconsultation; resolves handover discrepancies with Emergency Department before clearing. Hospital Liaison Desk (alias Kestrel): destination consultation, sends restrictions; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt; uses Pediatric Acuity Note with receiving staff; supports handover. Emergency Department; Riverside Trauma Center. Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias Bluejay): produces Battery Swap Voucher. Data Quality Officer (alias Pebble): sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo; reviews incomplete arrival/handover fields. Systems: Computer Aided Dispatch Console (displays surge level, constraints). Ambulance Coordination Platform. Regional Radio Network (en-route updates). Ambulance Unit 417 reports staging, arrival, handover complete. North Gate Status Board produces North Approach Queue Snapshot. South Gate Status Board produces South Access Lane Notice; displays south access info.

Document units:
S181: Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
S182: Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
S183: Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
S184: Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
S185: Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
S186: Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
S187: Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
S188: Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
S189: Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
S190: Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
S191: Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
S192: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
S193: Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
S194: Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
S195: North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
S196: South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
S197: After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
S198: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a degraded-radio procedure that prioritizes emergency traffic and preserves a common operating picture.
S199: Regional Radio Network operators announce channel outages, affected areas, and expected restoration times over the remaining service channels.
S200: Radio Coordinator directs crews to approved fallback channels when the primary channel is unusable.
S201: Crews acknowledge each fallback assignment and repeat critical location and destination details before moving.
